Two coders' GToBI labels

Source: R/data.R
tobi_agreement.Rd

Two trained coders label the same 456 words from 40 German utterances with GToBI pitch accents and phrase boundaries: 20 utterances of read and 20 of spontaneous speech. Coders agree on whether a word is accented about 85-90% of the time and on the type of accent about 60-70% of the time, close to published benchmarks for ToBI. Accent agreement is lower in spontaneous speech. For percentage agreement and Cohen's kappa.

Usage

tobi_agreement

Format

A tibble with 456 rows and 8 columns:

utterance

Utterance ID, U01 to U40.

style

"read" or "spontaneous".

word

Word ID (utterance_wNN).

position

Position of the word in the utterance.

accent_1, accent_2

Pitch accent labelled by coder 1 and coder 2: "none", "H*", "L+H*", "L*", "L*+H", "H+!H*" or "H+L*".

boundary_1, boundary_2

Boundary after the word labelled by coder 1 and coder 2: "none", "intermediate" or "intonation phrase".

Source

data-raw/tobi_agreement.R

Details

True model: each word has a true accent (55% none) and boundary (always an intonation phrase boundary at the end of the utterance, 12% intermediate boundaries elsewhere). Each coder gives the true label with probability plogis(base - difficulty), where base is 2.6 for unaccented and 1.6 for accented words (0.2 lower for coder 2) and the word's difficulty has mean 0 in read and 0.5 in spontaneous speech (SD 0.5). Otherwise the coder picks a similar label (e.g. "L+H*" for "H*").

References

Grice, M., Baumann, S. & Benzmüller, R. (2005). German intonation in autosegmental-metrical phonology. In S.-A. Jun (ed.), Prosodic Typology: The Phonology of Intonation and Phrasing (pp. 55-83). Oxford: Oxford University Press.

Pitrelli, J. F., Beckman, M. E. & Hirschberg, J. (1994). Evaluation of prosodic transcription labeling reliability in the ToBI framework. Proceedings of ICSLP 1994.

Examples

table(tobi_agreement$accent_1, tobi_agreement$accent_2)
#>        
#>         none  H* L+H*  L* L*+H H+!H* H+L*
#>   none   184  19    1  15    1     0    0
#>   H*      12  48    3   0    0     8    0
#>   L+H*     1  12   34   1   12     0    0
#>   L*      12   0    0  29    4     0    2
#>   L*+H     0   2    8   6   14     0    0
#>   H+!H*    1   8    0   0    0    11    2
#>   H+L*     0   1    0   0    0     1    4
